Announcement alert popup: current configured Windows PE decompilation

The four .c files in this directory are actual Ghidra 12.1.4 decompiler
output from the complete PE unwind owners, using the installed JDK 25.
They were obtained with tools/DecompileAnnouncementLog.java and a separate
temporary headless project for each configured edition. The original
instructions, literal operands, calls and conditional branches were read
again from the same disk images and retained alongside that output.
Generated names such as announcement_log_* and log_supplier_* belong to
the extraction script. Semantic field names below use the existing native
layout; they are not claimed to be symbols recovered from the stripped PE.

Images and complete owners:
  Steam/reference PE:6a70a6d9:02711000
    render 0x40d5f0..0x40f77a; input 0x40f780..0x4105a9
  Classic PE:6a70b91c:0270a000
    render 0x40b1b0..0x40d33a; input 0x40d340..0x40e169

Body-source precedence (reference-40d5f0.c; same Classic branches):
  owner+0xa8 != null: viewing_unit, category at owner+0xb0;
    read unit+0xce8+category*0x18 announcement-ID vector.
  otherwise owner+0x10 != 0: viewing_alert_button;
    read world.status.alert_button_announcement_id.
  otherwise owner+8 != null: selected alert;
    first read alert+8 announcement-ID vector;
    then read alert+0x20 unit-ID vector with its parallel categories.
  otherwise: no body source.
Each report ID is resolved against world.status.reports. Missing IDs are
skipped. Present records contribute the complete report.text at report+8.
The selected-alert unit branch similarly skips a missing unit; it has no
"Somebody" fallback. These are distinct from hover source construction.

The repeat branch is present separately in all three report paths:
  report.repeat_count at report+0x34 <= 0: use report.text unchanged;
  report.repeat_count > 0: copy report.text, append " x", then append the
    signed int32 decimal result of repeat_count+1 before wrapping.
  Reference instructions 0x40d812/0x40d82c,
    0x40dc7f/0x40dc99 and 0x40e0a0/0x40e0ba;
  Classic instructions 0x40b3d2/0x40b3ec,
    0x40b83f/0x40b859 and 0x40bc60/0x40bc7a.
The actual .c output contains all three <1 conditions and all three
integer-to-string calls. The suffix is display metadata, not an additional
announcement source production.

Unit-summary branch (reference 0x40e48d..0x40e50e):
  identity = unit full-name/profession formatter 0x1331500;
  capitalize identity, append " is ";
  category == 0: append "fighting!";
  category == 1: append "sparring.";
  category == 2: append "hunting.";
  every other category: append nothing.
The renderer does not reject an empty identity. The complete source forms
are therefore the three named summaries, the three empty-identity summaries,
and the named/empty invalid-category copula. Existing native unit identity
ownership and category handling in src/adventure_announcements.inc preserve
the field semantics, including empty names. The valid summary templates are
in data/runtime/ui-messages.tsv; invalid-category copulas add no activity.

Fixed instruction branches (native double spaces retained):
  viewing_unit, viewing_alert_button, or selected alert with no unit IDs:
    You can recenter on certain announcements.  Right click to close.
  selected alert with unit IDs:
    Select a report to view the full text.  Right click to close.
  no body owner: no instruction source.
The three emitted copies of the first instruction are the actual source
branches, not different translatable sentences. The instructions already
use complete-message translations in data/runtime/ui-messages.tsv.

The input functions manipulate scrolling, report selection, recentering,
unit/category selection and closing. Neither input owner contains an
authored text literal or constructs another visible sentence. Returning
from a selected unit clears owner+0xa8 when an alert parent remains;
otherwise closing clears the popup-active byte at owner+0.

All remaining rendered text is complete stored report.text; empty padding
rows and icon glyphs do not introduce sentences. Its native submission
universe is retained in the parent directory: native-announcement-enum.tsv,
native-submission-types.tsv, native-production-catalog.tsv and
native-scoped-productions.tsv, with the complete 235 producer owners and
their instruction branches. Generated proper names and user-authored
fields are typed inputs to those productions, not a finite list of names.

These artifacts are source extraction and decompilation evidence. They do
not describe a game-screen observation or a translation test result.
